svg.title: A child with a seizure: ABCDE and a bedside glucose and blood gas for every child, then fever and the seizure's features sort a simple from a complex febrile seizure, and a seizure past 5 minutes is convulsive status epilepticus treated by the clock with benzodiazepines, then a second-line load, then the intensive care unit

svg.text: EVERY child: bedside GLUCOSE + blood GAS with electrolytes

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: low glucose → IV dextrose (D10 5 mL/kg) · low sodium → 3% saline 3-5 mL/kg

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: subtle in newborns: lip smacking, eye deviation, bicycling, apnea, vital sign changes

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: FEVER, age 6 months-5 years: FEBRILE seizure

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: only if NO CNS infection, NO acute electrolyte problem, NO past afebrile seizure

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: WORRY: not back to baseline · meningeal signs or toxic look · delay or neurologic
